# Future Directions

## 1. Length-preserving Collatz inversion under a truncated domain

Conjecture: Fix a bit length `b`, sample `n` uniformly from `[2^{b-1},2^b)`, and reveal an encoded value of `T^a(n)` together with `a`. For a suitable relation between `a` and `b`, recovering any preimage in the same interval requires superpolynomial average-case time in a precisely specified branching-program model.

The key insight is that the universal preimage `2^a y` ceases to be admissible once inversion is required to preserve input length, so the reverse graph must navigate parity-dependent odd predecessors rather than follow only deterministic doubling edges.

Why now? The explicit unrestricted inverter identifies the exact boundary that a meaningful hardness statement must cross and reduces the next investigation to a concrete bounded-domain search problem.

## 2. Entropy of admissible reverse parity words

Conjecture: For targets `y` in a density-one subset of the natural numbers, the number of parity words of length `a` that encode a valid bounded preimage grows as `exp(ca+o(a))` for an explicit constant `c` strictly between zero and `log 2`.

The key insight is that reverse Collatz trajectories are governed by congruence constraints coupling division by three with parity, and their entropy—not forward convergence—is the plausible source of average-case search complexity.

Why now? The deterministic all-even reverse word is understood exactly, making it possible to separate that exceptional branch from the genuinely branching portion of the reverse tree.

## 3. Collision resistance after domain separation and compression

Conjecture: There exist explicit keyed affine domain separators and a length-preserving compression rule such that collisions inherited from `T(2k+1)=T(12k+8)` are excluded, while finding new collisions reduces to solving a quantified system of incompatible reverse-parity congruences.

The key insight is that raw Collatz iteration has algebraically parameterized collisions, so any credible construction must remove entire collision families structurally rather than hope that longer iteration hides them.

Why now? The persistent collision theorem supplies a complete adversarial test family against which candidate separators can be screened before any asymptotic security claim is attempted.

## 4. A generic obstruction theorem for dynamical one-way functions

Conjecture: In a standard uniform circuit model, any efficiently computable dynamical system possessing an efficiently computable section at every iterate fails distribution-free one-wayness, and any efficiently parameterized collision that is stable under iteration rules out collision resistance of the raw iterate family.

The key insight is that the Collatz counterexamples are instances of two abstract categorical structures—a section and a forward-stable kernel pair—that apply far beyond number-theoretic dynamics.

Why now? The two structures occur simultaneously in the Collatz map and can be isolated without assuming orbit convergence, providing a clean bridge between discrete dynamics, algebraic structure, and cryptographic definitions.

## 5. Separation of convergence from inversion complexity

Conjecture: There are explicit families of total maps on the natural numbers whose every positive orbit reaches a fixed point, yet whose bounded-domain inversion problems realize both polynomial-time and provably exponential query complexity depending only on their reverse-branch constraints.

The key insight is that forward termination controls orbit destinations but does not control the computational geometry of reverse fibers.

Why now? The unrestricted Collatz section demonstrates this logical separation sharply and motivates comparison families in which reverse complexity can be proved rather than inferred from empirical convergence.

exactly when the walk length is odd. -/
theorem dipole_walk_parity {k : ℕ} {a b : OrbitalState}
    (w : DipoleWalk k a b) : (a.l + b.l) % 2 = k % 2 := by
  induction w with
  | nil a => omega
  | @cons k a b c hab hbc ih =>
      unfold DipoleAllowed at hab
      rcases hab.1 with h | h <;> omega

/-- An odd-length closed dipole walk cannot exist.  Equivalently, the dipole
transition graph has no odd cycle. -/
theorem no_odd_closed_dipole_walk {k : ℕ} {a : OrbitalState}
    (hk : Odd k) : ¬ DipoleWalk k a a := by
  intro w
  have hp := dipole_walk_parity w
  obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := hk
  omega

/-- Two successive dipole transitions return to the original parity class. -/
theorem two_step_preserves_parity {a b c : OrbitalState}
    (hab : DipoleAllowed a b) (hbc : DipoleAllowed b c) :
    parityColor a = parityColor c := by
  have w : DipoleWalk 2 a c := by
    simpa using DipoleWalk.cons hab (DipoleWalk.cons hbc (DipoleWalk.nil c))
  have hp := dipole_walk_parity w
  apply Fin.ext
  simp only [parityColor]
  omega

end HydrogenSpectralConnector

# Computational evidence

## Small cases

In Rydberg units the first four bound levels are

| principal number `n` | `-1/n²` |
|---:|---:|
| 1 | -1 |
| 2 | -1/4 |
| 3 | -1/9 |
| 4 | -1/16 |

These exact calculations are machine-checked by `first_four_bound_energies` in
`HydrogenSpectralConnector.lean`.  They increase and remain negative, consistent
with convergence to the ionization threshold zero; the universal monotonicity
and convergence claims are also proved there.

For orbital angular momentum, allowed `Δl = ±1` transitions alternate parity:
`0 → 1 → 2 → 3`.  A two-step path returns to the initial parity, while a
three-step path changes it.  The theorem `dipole_walk_parity` proves this for
every finite path, not merely these examples.

## OEIS search

The shell degeneracies `1, 4, 9, 16, ...` are the square numbers, OEIS A000290.
The present connector focuses on transition-graph parity rather than reproving
the standard shell-degeneracy sum.

## Counterexample hunt

Potential edge cases are `l = 0`, equal endpoints, and walks that backtrack.
The condition `Δl = ±1` excludes equal-`l` edges, including `0 → 0`; backtracking
gives an even closed walk and is correctly permitted.  No odd closed walk can
occur, as proved by `no_odd_closed_dipole_walk`.

## Table of path parity

| number of dipole steps | endpoint parity relation |
|---:|:---|
| 0 | same |
| 1 | different |
| 2 | same |
| 3 | different |
| `k` | different exactly when `k` is odd |

open Catalog.ProofAutomation.Fibonacci

/-- Finite gcds commute with the Fibonacci map.  Thus the binary strong
Divisibility identity extends to every finite family of indices. -/
theorem finset_gcd_fib (s : Finset ℕ) :
    s.gcd Nat.fib = Nat.fib (s.gcd id) := by
  induction s using Finset.induction_on with
  | empty => simp
  | @insert a s ha ih =>
      rw [Finset.gcd_insert, Finset.gcd_insert, ih]
      exact Fib_gcd_identity a (s.gcd id)

/-- A number divides all Fibonacci values in a finite family exactly when it
Divides the Fibonacci value at the gcd of that family. -/
theorem dvd_fib_finset_gcd_iff (p : ℕ) (s : Finset ℕ) :
    p ∣ Nat.fib (s.gcd id) ↔ ∀ n ∈ s, p ∣ Nat.fib n := by
  rw [← finset_gcd_fib s]
  exact Finset.dvd_gcd_iff

/-- At a sufficiently large prime index, Carmichael primitivity upgrades to an
exact global apparition law: one prime divisor appears precisely at multiples
of that index. -/
theorem prime_index_exact_fib_apparition (q : ℕ) (hq : Nat.Prime q)
    (hq13 : 13 ≤ q) :
    ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ ∀ m, p ∣ Nat.fib m ↔ q ∣ m := by
  rcases fib_primitive_divisor_prime q hq13 hq with ⟨p, hp, hpq, hprimitive⟩
  refine ⟨p, hp, fun m => ?_⟩
  constructor
  · intro hpm
    by_contra hnot
    have hgcd_dvd : p ∣ Nat.fib (Nat.gcd q m) := by
      rw [← Fib_gcd_identity]
      exact Nat.dvd_gcd hpq hpm
    rcases hq.eq_one_or_self_of_dvd (Nat.gcd q m) (Nat.gcd_dvd_left q m) with hgcd | hgcd
    · rw [hgcd, Nat.fib_one] at hgcd_dvd
      exact hp.not_dvd_one hgcd_dvd
    · exact hnot (hgcd ▸ Nat.gcd_dvd_right q m)
  · intro hqm
    exact dvd_trans hpq (Nat.fib_dvd q m hqm)

/-- **Finite synchronization theorem.** For a prime Fibonacci index `q ≥ 13`,
there is a prime `p` such that, simultaneously for every finite set of indices,
`p` divides the gcd of the corresponding Fibonacci numbers exactly when `q`
divides the gcd of the indices. -/
theorem fibonacci_prime_finset_synchronization (q : ℕ) (hq : Nat.Prime q)
    (hq13 : 13 ≤ q) :
    ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ ∀ s : Finset ℕ,
      p ∣ s.gcd Nat.fib ↔ q ∣ s.gcd id := by
  rcases prime_index_exact_fib_apparition q hq hq13 with ⟨p, hp, happ⟩
  refine ⟨p, hp, fun s => ?_⟩
  rw [Finset.dvd_gcd_iff, Finset.dvd_gcd_iff]
  constructor
  · intro hall n hn
    exact (happ n).mp (hall n hn)
  · intro hall n hn
    exact (happ n).mpr (hall n hn)
